glance_takeaway: This page is an onboarding map of 'meridian', a self-hosted read-later/RSS service with a Python backend, SQLite store, HTTP API, vanilla-JS reader, and CLI. Its main message is that the system is a one-way ingest pipeline (scheduler -> fetcher -> extractor -> dedup -> store -> full-text index) writing into a single SQLite database that the API, web reader, and CLI read back out of; a newcomer's first change will land in pipeline/sources/ or api/routes.py, and pipeline/extractor.py is the file to treat with caution. The repo is ~23k lines split into six backend packages, with a module table showing LOC and coverage per package.

F1.note: Module table lists all six packages (pipeline, api, store, render, queue, cli) plus shared layer; web/ paragraph: 'no framework, no build step'.

F2.note: Bold exec summary: 'scheduler -> fetcher -> extractor -> dedup -> store -> full-text index'; expanded in 'How data moves'.

F3.note: Invariant 2: 'Every INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE in the codebase lives in that one 610-LOC file; everything else reads through store/reader.py.'

F4.note: Invariant 1: 'Bytes in -> Article out; no network, disk, DB, or clock. The same HTML always yields the same Article.'

F5.note: Caution callout: extractor.py line 41 imports clean_html() from render/sanitize.py, sideways edge since v0.8, tracked as issue #214.

F6.note: Layering paragraph: 'store/ sits at the bottom and imports no other meridian package... And nothing imports api/ or cli/.'

F7.note: 'The one scary file' section: largest file at 1,140 LOC, 14 site-specific extraction heuristics inlined as if/elif chains.

F8.note: Shape section: '13,710 LOC of backend Python'; table shows pipeline/ at 4,180 LOC as the largest module.

F9.note: Tests section: '77% overall... store 91%... cli 41%'; caution callout: 'The frontend has no automated tests at all — 0%'.

F10.note: Tests section: '412 tests total (348 unit + 64 integration), running in ~41 s locally.'

F11.note: Write path: '64-bit simhash... Hamming distance <= 3... about 7% of incoming items are dropped this way.'

F12.note: Numbered 4-file recipe lists exactly base.py, __init__.py, store/migrations/, cli/commands/add.py (fixture test noted as an addition, consistent with the recipe framing).

F13.note: Write path: SQLite jobs table, broker leases to 8 worker threads, typical depth 30-60, health endpoint alerts at 500; table row: 'No Redis, no Celery.'

F14.note: Read path: api/routes.py -> store/reader.py (6 ms) -> render/template.py (14 ms) -> render/annotations.py (8 ms); 'Total p50: 28 ms.'

F15.note: Invariant 3: 'Only SQLite triggers in schema.sql touch articles_fts'; write path repeats 'application code never writes the index.'

strengths: Perfect factual fidelity: all 15 ground-truth facts are conveyed, most with exact numbers, and negative facts (layering violation, xfail purity tests, 0% frontend coverage) are given visual prominence via caution callouts rather than sanded off.

Strong above-the-fold executive summary: the bolded lede compresses T1, T2, and half of T3 into one legible paragraph, so a 10-second glance yields the shape, the two first-change locations, and the file to fear.
Well-chosen prose ordering (shape -> data flow -> rules -> hotspots -> first change -> tests) that matches how a new contributor would actually onboard, ending with a genuine 'In short' recap.
weaknesses: No diagram for an intrinsically diagrammatic subject: the one-way pipeline, hub-and-spoke store, and import-layering DAG are all described only in running prose, forcing the reader to build the picture mentally.
The invariants (T4) and the reason extractor.py is scary (T3's specifics) live below the fold and do not survive a glance; the glance carries facts but not the discipline story.
Long unbroken paragraphs (e.g. the four-stage write path is one ~12-line paragraph packing five facts) hurt re-findability; no table of contents or anchor navigation for a page this long.

Visual encoding is minimal: one table and two callout styles carry all the structure; LOC and coverage numbers are never encoded visually (no bars, no emphasis on the 41%/62% outliers in the table itself).
evaluator_notes: A textbook prose baseline: maximally accurate (accuracy is mechanically 10.0 since 15/15 facts are conveyed and none distorted or contradicted) and honestly caveated, but it spends almost nothing on visual conveyance. The glance succeeds on T1/T2 because the author front-loaded a bolded summary sentence, not because of any visual design. Deep comprehension is high for a motivated developer but 2-3 minutes is tight for ~1,600 words; the pipeline order, layering rules, and hotspot rationale would land faster and stick better with even one diagram. Scored per rubric v1: overall = 0.35*10.0 + 0.30*7.0 + 0.15*7.5 + 0.10*6.5 + 0.10*5.5 = 7.925 -> 7.9.
